leksikon_evidence: 2 bare-surname mentions, no heading: vol.3 "מוזיק פֿון מינקאָווסקי" (person_description: קאָמפּאָזיטאָר); vol.1 "דעם 25 דעצעמבער 1890 — זיין היסטאָרישע פּאָלנישע אָפּערע — דער יידישער פּאָלקאָווניק [בערעק יאָסעלעוויטש], מוזיק פֿון מאָגולעסקאָ און מינקאָווסקי". Catalogue cites locators 2:971, 3:2151.
primary_attestation: Ronald Robboy, "Reconstructing a Yiddish Theatre Score: Giacomo Minkowski and His Music to Alexander; or, the Crown Prince of Jerusalem", in Joel Berkowitz & Barbara Henry (eds), Inventing the Modern Yiddish Stage (Wayne State UP, 2012). Digital Yiddish Theatre Project: immigrant from Odessa, arrived New York early 1890s, wrote several scores to Lateiner operettas starring Boris Thomashefsky; born Yankele, renamed after Giacomo Meyerbeer.
corroborating_people: 685 Sigmund Mogulesco (co-credited on the 1890 premiere); 683 Joseph Lateiner; 693 Boris Thomashefsky
open_questions: Distinct from the Odessa cantor Pinchas/Pinye Minkowski (1859-1924) and his father ר' מאָטל, who account for the other 14 lexicon mentions. NO evidence of a sibling relation between them — an earlier guess to that effect was withdrawn.

leksikon_evidence: No heading. Five Simovitch mentions exist (אַברהם, שלום, סימאָוויטש) but ALL are male actors; no Amy/Emmy in the Leksikon.
primary_attestation: Advertisement in Di Thalia (New York), 17 April 1896, crediting her as actress in Lateiner's Blimele (di Perle von Warsha) at the Thalia Theatre. Given name confirmed as איימי = Amy by Sinai from the ad itself, 2026-10-05.
corroborating_people: 3264 Mary Wilensky (same Blimele production); 878 Max Rosenthal (same production, 1896-05-08)
open_questions: Relation (if any) to the Leksikon's Simovitch family — 715 Abraham, 2983 Regina [Kubowitz], 2984 Sholem — is unestablished. Regina Simovitsh married the actor Sholem Simovitch and played in Bucharest.

leksikon_evidence: No heading of her own. Of 360 Kaminska mentions, the Leksikon headings are her parents and sister: 3610 Esther-Rokhl [Halpern], 3613 Avrom-Yitskhok, 3612 Regina.
primary_attestation: Advertisement in Haynt, 18 November 1938, crediting her as Sore Sheyndel in a Warsaw performance of Lateiner's Di farblondzhete neshome. Biography: 1899-1980, daughter of Esther-Rokhl and Avrom-Yitskhok Kamiński; directed her own Drama Theater in Warsaw until 1939.
corroborating_people: 3610 Esther-Rokhl Kaminska (mother); 3613 Avrom-Yitskhok Kaminski (father); 3612 Regina Kaminska (sister)
open_questions: OUT OF PERIOD for this corpus: the credit is a 1938 revival, 23 years after the Lateiner/Hurwitz editions end. Minted as a person in her own right, not as a corpus-period participant — do not read the Sore Sheyndel credit as contemporaneous with the edition.

leksikon_evidence: No heading of his own. Mentioned as "אַדאָלף ליאַנסקי", described אַקטיאָר און דירעקטאָר (actor and director), staging a comedy with אָדעלאָ ליאַנסקי in 1910 (volume_2IIIorg). The Leksikon shows a Liansky family: Adolf, Odelo (director, female), הערש ליאַנסקי (= people_db 3725, distinct person, confirmed by Sinai 2026-10-06) and an unnamed member of Kalman Yoliver's troupe.
primary_attestation: Ownership inscription on the title page (p.3) of the Ben HaDor manuscript: "Eigentum A. Liansky, New-Jork, 7. October 1904". He is the only A. Liansky in the Leksikon, and a director owning a prompt-book fits the inscription.
corroborating_people: 3725 Hersch Liansky (family, distinct person); 684 Moyshe Hurwitz (author of the owned MS)
open_questions: Relation to Hersch (3725) and Odelo is familial but unspecified in the sources. Odelo Liansky is NOT in people_db and may warrant minting separately.
